summary: Hungary is part of the EU and the Schengen Area: EU and EFTA citizens enter freely, around 60 visa-exempt nationalities can stay 90 days in any 180-day period (with the ETIAS travel authorisation being phased in), and everyone else needs a Schengen short-stay visa costing €90.

visaTypes.name: National Long-Stay Visa (Type D) / Residence Permit

fee.notes: For stays over 90 days: work, study, family and other long-stay purposes, usually processed together with a residence permit. Fees vary by category.
For courses longer than 90 days; needs proof of enrolment at a Hungarian institution, accommodation, funds and health insurance.
Combined residence and work authorisation for employment over 90 days; requires a contract with an employer in Hungary and is initiated before travel.

passportValidity.text: Non-EU passports must be valid for at least 3 months beyond your planned departure from the Schengen Area and have been issued within the last 10 years.

travelInsurance.text: Schengen visa applicants must hold travel medical insurance covering at least €30,000, valid across the Schengen Area for the whole stay. Visa-exempt visitors are not required to show it but border officers may ask about cover.

onwardTicket.text: Border officers may ask non-EU visitors for proof of return or onward travel and accommodation details.

proofOfFunds.text: Non-EU visitors may be asked to show sufficient funds — commonly cited as around 10,000 HUF per person per day — plus proof of accommodation and means to leave the country.

declarations.name: EES — Entry/Exit System (biometric registration)
declarations.submitWindow: At the border on first entry
declarations.text: Non-EU travellers are registered biometrically (fingerprints and photo) in the EU Entry/Exit System at Schengen external borders. Registration happens at the border — there is nothing to submit in advance, but allow extra time on your first entry.

declarations.name: ETIAS — European Travel Information and Authorisation System

fee.notes: Free for under-18s and over-70s. Valid 3 years or until passport expiry.

declarations.text: Visa-exempt travellers will need an ETIAS travel authorisation to enter the Schengen Area. It is being phased in — check the official EU site for the current status and apply only there.

currencyLimits.text: Cash of €10,000 or more (or equivalent) must be declared when entering or leaving the EU.

notes: Duty-free from outside the EU: 200 cigarettes, 1 litre of spirits, goods up to €300 (€430 arriving by air/sea).
No limits on goods for personal use when arriving from another EU country.
Full border checks apply when crossing to and from Serbia and Ukraine — these are external Schengen borders.

payments.text: Cards and contactless payments are accepted almost everywhere in cities, including transport and baths. Hungary does not use the euro — pay in forint and decline dynamic currency conversion.

safety.text: Hungary is one of Europe's safest destinations. The main risks for visitors are pickpocketing on Budapest transport and around sights, and overcharging by unofficial taxis and some bars.

source.name: U.S. Department of State — Hungary Travel Advisory

bestTimeToVisit.text: April–June and September–October offer pleasant weather in Budapest and around Lake Balaton without the summer heat; December brings Christmas markets and steamy outdoor thermal baths.

tips.text: The 90-day limit counts across the entire Schengen Area, not just Hungary — days spent in Austria or Slovakia count against the same allowance.

In Budapest use only official yellow taxis with a company logo and fixed government tariff, or apps like Bolt and Főtaxi — freelance taxis hailed near sights and clubs are known for heavy overcharging.

At thermal baths (Széchenyi, Gellért, Rudas) bring a swimsuit, towel and flip-flops; a swim cap is required only in swimming-lap pools. Lockers and cabins are included or rentable — book popular baths online in high season.
Always choose to pay in forint (HUF), not your home currency, at card terminals and ATMs, and avoid exchange offices with wide rate spreads around tourist areas.

faq.question: Do US citizens need a visa for Hungary?
faq.answer: No. US passport holders can visit Hungary and the rest of the Schengen Area visa-free for up to 90 days in any 180-day period. Once ETIAS becomes mandatory, they will need to obtain this online authorisation (€20) before travel.

faq.question: How much does a Hungary Schengen visa cost?
faq.answer: The Schengen short-stay visa costs €90 for adults and €45 for children aged 6–11. It allows stays of up to 90 days in any 180-day period across all Schengen countries, and applications are decided within 15–45 calendar days.

faq.question: Does Hungary use the euro?
faq.answer: No. Hungary uses the Hungarian forint (HUF). Cards are accepted almost everywhere, including the Budapest metro and thermal baths; when paying by card or withdrawing cash, always choose to be charged in forint.

faq.question: Is ETIAS required to enter Hungary?
faq.answer: ETIAS is being phased in for visa-exempt travellers. During the transition period travellers without ETIAS are still admitted; once fully mandatory, the €20 online authorisation will be required before boarding. Check the official EU website for the current status.

faq.question: How long can I stay in Hungary without a visa?
faq.answer: Visa-exempt non-EU visitors can stay up to 90 days within any 180-day period, counted across the whole Schengen Area. EU and EFTA citizens can stay indefinitely but must register locally after 3 months.
